h1: The 8 Best Upright Vacuums for Carpet Cleaning, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Upright Vacuums for Carpet: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 upright vacuums for carpet from Shark, Kenmore, Bissell, Sanitaire and Oreck, compared on filtration, bags and pet tools.
summary: The Shark NV752 Rotator is the upright most carpeted homes should buy, with a powered Lift-Away design, a pet power brush and a HEPA filter. The Kenmore Elite 31150 is the best bagged choice for allergy households, the Sanitaire Force is the commercial workhorse, and the Bissell Pet Hair Eraser is the strongest mid-priced pet option.
intro: Most upright vacuum shopping goes wrong at the first question. Buyers ask how strong the suction is, when carpet cleaning is mostly decided by the brush roll and how well the machine seals. Suction without agitation just lifts the surface layer of a rug, while a good beater bar loosens grit that has worked into the pile.

We ranked eight uprights, from commercial bagged models to pet-focused bagless machines, using the features each listing names: HEPA filtration, bag or bin design, height adjustment, pet tools and commercial build. Where a listing gives no specs, as with some Sanitaire and Oreck models, we say so instead of filling the gap with guesses.

products.name: Shark NV752 Rotator Powered Lift-Away TruePet Upright Vacuum with HEPA Filter, Large Dust Cup Capacity, LED Headlights, Upholstery Tool, Perfect Pet Power Brush & Crevice Tool, Bordeaux
products.verdict: The best all-rounder, with a powered Lift-Away, a HEPA filter and pet tools.
products.description:
The NV752 is a bagless upright with a Powered Lift-Away design, a HEPA filter, a large dust cup and LED headlights. It comes with an upholstery tool, a Perfect Pet Power Brush and a crevice tool.

It ranks first because it handles both big rooms and the small jobs that follow. Lift-Away means the pod detaches from the base so you can clean stairs or furniture without a second vacuum. Powered means the brush roll keeps spinning in this mode. LED headlights help you spot hair and crumbs on dark carpet. The tradeoff against the bagged Kenmore is that you empty a dust cup by hand, which sends fine dust into the air.

Buy it if you have pets and mixed floors. Skip it if you are sensitive to dust and prefer a sealed bag.

products.name: Kenmore Elite 31150 Pet Friendly Bagged Upright Beltless Vacuum w/Pet Handi-Mate, Triple HEPA, 3D Inducer Motor, Telescoping Wand, 5-Position Height Adjustment, 3 Cleaning Tools-Silver
products.verdict: Bagged, beltless and Triple HEPA with 5 height positions.
products.description:
The Kenmore Elite 31150 is a bagged, beltless upright with Triple HEPA filtration, a 3D inducer motor, a telescoping wand, a Pet Handi-Mate and five height positions. Three cleaning tools are included.

It ranks second because a sealed bag is the best design for people with allergies, since the dust goes into the bag and stays there when you throw it out. Beltless means no drive belt to stretch or snap, a common failure point. Five-position height adjustment suits low shag, standard pile and bare floors. It sits behind the Shark because it does not have a Lift-Away pod, and bags are an ongoing cost.

Choose it if you want a sealed system and strong filtration. Skip it if you dislike buying bags.
products.idealFor: Allergy households and owners with several carpet types.
products.skipIf: You would rather not buy replacement bags.

products.name: Sanitaire Force Upright Commercial Vacuum SC5845D,Black
products.verdict: A commercial-grade upright built for heavy daily carpet use.
products.description:
The Sanitaire Force SC5845D is a commercial upright vacuum. The listing gives few specifications, but the commercial classification signals a machine designed for offices, hotels and rental properties.

It ranks third because commercial uprights prize durability and straightforward serviceability over features. They generally have a metal or heavy-duty frame, easy-to-swap bags and belts, and a simple switch layout. What you give up compared with a home model is the tool set and pet attachments. It costs between $200 and $500, which is on par with the Shark and Kenmore.

Buy it if you clean a lot of carpet and want a no-fuss machine. Skip it if you need attachments for stairs and upholstery.
products.idealFor: Owners who vacuum a lot of wall-to-wall carpet.
products.skipIf: You need stair and upholstery tools.

products.name: Bissell Pet Hair Eraser Allergen Lift-Off, HEPA, 39883
products.verdict: A HEPA pet upright with a Lift-Off pod, at a mid-range price.
products.description:
The Bissell Pet Hair Eraser Allergen Lift-Off 39883 pairs a HEPA filter with a Lift-Off pod, aimed at pet owners. The listing does not spell out its other features.

It ranks fourth because it offers the pet-hair focus of the Shark at a lower price, in the $100 to $200 bucket. The Lift-Off design lets you take the canister with you for stairs and upholstery. It loses ground on the unlisted details, so we cannot compare brush roll design, cord length or tool count with the Shark.

Choose it if you want pet-focused cleaning without the Shark's price. Skip it if you want documented extras such as headlights and a pet power brush.
products.idealFor: Pet owners on a mid-range budget.
products.skipIf: You want a full documented tool kit.

products.name: Shark Navigator Lift-Away Vacuum, HEPA, Pet Hair, White/Silver, NV356E
products.verdict: A lower-cost Lift-Away with HEPA and a pet hair focus.
products.description:
The Navigator NV356E is a Lift-Away upright with a HEPA filter and a pet hair focus, in white and silver. It is the lower-priced Shark in this ranking, at $100 to $200.

It ranks fifth because it is a simpler machine than the Rotator above: no powered Lift-Away is listed, no headlights and no dedicated pet brush. The core idea is the same, though, with a canister that comes off the base for above-floor cleaning. For a carpeted apartment it covers the basics.

Buy it if you want the Shark approach on a smaller budget. Skip it if you want a powered brush roll when you lift the pod away.
cons: No headlights or power brush listed
products.idealFor: Apartment dwellers wanting a Shark on a budget.
products.skipIf: You want the most powerful pet brush.

products.name: Oreck Commercial Upright Vacuum Cleaner, LEED Compliant
products.verdict: A commercial upright that meets LEED criteria.
products.description:
The Oreck Commercial Upright is described as LEED compliant, a reference to the green building program that sets rules for cleaning equipment in certified buildings. The listing names few other features.

It ranks sixth because compliance is helpful for offices that chase certification, but it does not tell a homeowner much about carpet performance. Pricing lands alongside the Sanitaire Force at $200 to $500, and that machine offers a more conventional commercial build.

Choose it if a facility needs LEED-compliant equipment. Skip it for home use, where the Shark or Kenmore deliver more.
cons: No pet or stair tools mentioned
products.idealFor: Offices and facilities needing LEED-compliant equipment.
products.skipIf: You are buying for a home with pets.

products.name: Sanitaire SC679K Tradition Upright Commercial Bagged Vacuum, Red
products.verdict: A bagged commercial upright at the lower end of the price range.
products.description:
The SC679K Tradition is a bagged commercial upright, finished in red, in the $100 to $200 bucket. As with the Force, the listing is light on specs.

It ranks seventh because a bagged commercial machine is a sensible, low-cost way to clean carpet but is not a feature-rich choice. The Tradition name hints at a basic design that trades extras for simplicity. Bags keep dust contained, and replacements for Sanitaire uprights are widely stocked.

Buy it if you want a no-frills bagged upright for plain carpet. Skip it if you have pets or need above-floor tools.
products.idealFor: Plain carpeted rooms and rental units.
products.skipIf: You have pets or need stair attachments.

products.name: Oreck Commercial XL Vacuum Cleaner, Bagged Upright Vac, Lightweight
products.verdict: A lightweight bagged upright for those who find heavy vacuums tiring.
products.description:
The Oreck Commercial XL is a lightweight bagged upright in the $100 to $200 bucket. Lightness is its selling point, and the listing does not name filtration or height adjustment.

It ranks last because weight savings often come with a trade in power or durability, and the listing does not offer evidence either way. It is a plain machine for easy carrying, more suited to hard floors and low pile than deep shag.

Choose it if you struggle to push or carry a heavy upright. Skip it for thick carpet or large homes.
cons: Light build suits low pile only
products.idealFor: People who want an easy-to-lift vacuum for light carpet.
products.skipIf: You have deep pile or a large house.

whatMatters.detail: On carpet, the rotating brush roll does the real work by loosening embedded grit. A vacuum with strong suction but a weak brush leaves dirt in the pile. Look for a motorized brush and, on pet models, a dedicated pet power brush as on the Shark NV752.

Bagged uprights seal dust inside a bag that you throw away, which is better for allergies. Bagless models avoid ongoing bag costs but release fine dust when you empty the bin. If dust bothers you, favor the Kenmore Elite or a commercial bagged unit.

A HEPA filter captures 99.97 percent of particles down to 0.3 micron when the machine is sealed. Triple HEPA, as on the Kenmore Elite, adds more stages. Check the listing for a sealed system, since a leaky body can defeat even a good filter.

Different carpets need different brush heights. A low setting suits thin pile, while a high setting stops a machine from sticking on shag. The Kenmore Elite offers five positions, which is why it ranks so well for mixed homes.

Uprights are heavy, and a machine that you cannot carry upstairs is a poor fit for a multi-level home. A Lift-Away pod or telescoping wand helps with stairs and furniture. Check which tools are in the box before you buy.

faq.q: Are commercial uprights good for homes?
faq.a: Yes, for people who value durability and simple controls over attachments. They tend to be sturdier but come with fewer tools. Pet owners will probably prefer the Shark or Bissell.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying an upright vacuum?
faq.a: Focusing on suction instead of brush roll and sealing. Carpet needs agitation to release embedded dirt, and a leaky machine blows dust back out. Check the brush design and filtration.

faq.q: Is the Shark NV752 worth it over the Navigator?
faq.a: For pets and stairs, yes. The Rotator adds a powered Lift-Away, headlights and a pet power brush. The Navigator is fine for basic carpet at a lower price.

faq.q: How do I set the right carpet height?
faq.a: Start at the lowest setting that lets the machine glide, and raise it if it grabs or stalls. The Kenmore Elite has five positions, so you can fit thin pile and thick shag.

faq.q: How often should I replace the filter or bag?
faq.a: Replace bags when they are about two thirds full, and wash or replace filters as the manual directs, typically every few months. A full bag cuts suction long before it is actually full.

faq.q: Can I use these on hard floors too?
faq.a: Some can, but a spinning brush roll may scatter debris on bare floors. Look for a brush-off switch or a height setting for bare floors before using an upright on tile or wood.

finalTake: The Shark NV752 Rotator is the upright most carpeted homes should buy, thanks to its powered Lift-Away, HEPA filter and pet brush. The Kenmore Elite 31150 is the better call for allergies, and the Sanitaire Force suits heavy daily use. The Bissell and Shark Navigator keep costs down. Choose by brush roll, filtration and household first, then price.
